identity.title: First Abundance Measurement of Organic Molecules in the Atmosphere of HH 212 Protostellar Disk

paper_type_evidence.quote: The HH 212 protostellar system was observed with ALMA in Band 7 at $\sim$ 341.5 GHz in Cycle 5. Project ID was 2017.1.00044.S.

evidence.quote: HH 212 is a young Class 0 protostellar system deeply embedded in a compact molecular cloud core in the L1630 cloud of Orion at a distance of $\sim$ 400 pc (cite: Kounkel2017).
HH 212 is a young Class 0 protostellar system deeply embedded in a compact molecular cloud core in the L1630 cloud of Orion at a distance of $\sim$ 400 pc (cite: Kounkel2017).

question.value: Which organic molecules are present in the HH 212 protostellar disk atmosphere, what are their abundances, and how do they compare with hot corinos around other protostars?

evidence.quote: we report the first systematic survey and abundance measurement of organic molecules in the disk atmosphere within $\sim$ 40 au of the central protostar.
Project ID was 2017.1.00044.S.
The HH 212 protostellar system was observed with ALMA in Band 7 at $\sim$ 341.5 GHz in Cycle 5.

analysis_steps.goal: Make continuum and line channel maps

method.value: Calibrate in CASA, image with robust 0.5, subtract continuum from line-free channels

evidence.quote: We used a robust factor of 0.5 for the visibility weighting to generate the channel maps

analysis_steps.goal: Identify lines and map molecular emission

method.value: Use position-frequency diagrams along the lower atmosphere to identify lines with the linear PF structure; stack unblended detected lines per species into mean intensity maps

evidence.quote: we stacked the line intensity maps in different transitions, excluding those tentatively detected (marked with T) and blended (marked with B)

analysis_steps.goal: Derive excitation temperature and column densities

method.value: Rotation diagrams in the optically thin limit for lines measured in a rectangular region (0.2" x 0.05") of the lower atmosphere (2 sigma cutoff, lines >3 sigma); fixed T=150+-50 K for other molecules; single lines from integrated intensity

evidence.quote: Here we derive the mean excitation temperature and column density in the disk atmosphere by fitting the rotation diagram of the molecular lines.
The line intensities here are assumed to have an uncertainty of 40%.

assumptions.value: Optically thin lines, mean Tex 150+-50 K for molecules with weak lines

evidence.quote: Assuming this mean temperature for the disk atmosphere, we can estimate the column densities of other molecules with weaker lines.

validation.value: Upper atmosphere temperatures checked: 138+-32 K (CH3OH), 168+-24 K (CH2DOH)

evidence.quote: we also obtained similar temperatures of $\sim$ $138\pm32$ K and $\sim$ $168\pm24$ K for the upper atmosphere

method.value: Remove expected CH2DCN contamination (~21 K km/s, ~18%) from 13CH3OH line and multiply 13CH3OH column by 12C/13C = 50

evidence.quote: it is estimated to be $\sim$ 21 K km s$^{-1}$, or $\sim$ 18% of the total intensity there.
a $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio of 50 as obtained in the Orion Complex (cite: Kahane2018)

validation.value: Derived CH3OH column about twice the rotation-diagram value, indicating optically thick CH3OH lines

evidence.quote: the CH$_3$OH column density derived this way is about twice that derived from the rotation diagram, suggesting that the CH$_3$OH lines are indeed optically thick.

method.value: Divide column densities by mean H2 column 3.8e24 cm^-2; compare abundances relative to CH3CHO with other hot corinos

evidence.quote: the abundances of the molecules, as listed in Table [2](#tab:colabun), can be obtained by dividing the column density of the molecules by this mean H$_2$ column density.

assumptions.value: Dust optical depth tau<~1, so columns could be underestimated by factor e; abundances uncertain by a factor of a few due to dust opacity

evidence.quote: The abundances here can be uncertain by a factor a few because the mean H$_2$ column density depends on dust opacity

validation.value: Relative abundances similar to other hot corinos within a factor of few

evidence.quote: the relative abundances of most molecules here in HH 212 are similar to those in other hot corinos to within a factor of few

findings_qualitative.value: Molecular emission is only in the upper and lower disk atmosphere, brighter below the midplane, within the centrifugal barrier (~0.11", 44 au)

evidence.quote: Molecular line emissions are only detected in the upper (above the midplane) and lower disk atmosphere, with the emission brighter in the lower disk atmosphere below the midplane.
